about: Check-in chat replies for measure-chat.mjs (made-up students), several runs per case. Regenerate with --refresh rather than edit.

gigs, rules out sport.ask: Gigs and live music. Not sport. A gig, then out with mates. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: Since you like live music, you might enjoy Gigs or the Music society, and Habita is a great spot to hang out with mates afterwards.

homebody, rules out partying.ask: Board games and reading. Not partying. A quiet night in with a film. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: Since you mentioned board games, Gaming and Roleplay is a great fit. For reading, you might like Book, and Film suits your interest in a quiet night in with a movie.

sporty early riser.ask: Football and the gym. Up early for a run, then football. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: It sounds like you have a very active routine. You might like Football, Futsal, or Sport.
notes: Likes football, going to the gym, and getting up early for a run

lie-in and the cinema.ask: Photography and the cinema. A lie-in, then the cinema. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: For your interests, you might enjoy Film for cinema fans, as well as Art and Creative Corridor if you like photography. Is there anything you'd like reminding about while you settle in?

gamer, last minute (near tie).ask: Gaming, Minecraft and FIFA. Gaming online late with mates. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: Since you are into gaming, Minecraft, and FIFA, you might like Video Game, Esports, or Gaming and Roleplay.

clubbing (synonyms for partying).ask: Going clubbing and festivals. Big nights out. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: For big nights out and clubbing, Dance and Sync DJ are great societies to join, and Habita is the main student bar on campus. Is there anything you would like reminding about while you settle in?
notes: Likes clubbing, festivals and big nights out

outdoors, rules out the gym.ask: Hiking and climbing. Not the gym. Up early for a long walk. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: Since you are into hiking, climbing, and long walks, you might like Mountaineering, Walking, or Climbing. Their cards have all the details on how to join.
notes: Enjoys hiking, climbing, and long walks, but not the gym

unrelated to every mentor.ask: Knitting and birdwatching. A trip to a nature reserve. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: For knitting, Stitch, Make & Bitch and Hooked By Crochet are both great societies to check out.
notes: Likes knitting and birdwatching, and wants to go on a trip to a nature reserve

only says what they don't want in 3 answ.ask: I'm not into sport, clubbing or gaming. I don't like loud nights out. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: There are lots of other societies to try out instead, like arts, crafts or academic groups. You can browse the full list of societies on the Students' Union pages to see what catches your eye.

quiet nights in, not nights out (opposit.ask: Reading and films. Quiet nights in, not nights out. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: For quiet nights in, you might enjoy Book or Film, as they are great for sharing those relaxing interests.
notes: Enjoys reading, films and quiet nights in rather than nights out

live music (synonym for gigs).ask: Live music, mostly indie bands. Seeing a band, then drinks with friends. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: Since you enjoy live music and indie bands, you might like the Music society and the Rock society, and for drinks with friends you could try Habita.
notes: Likes live music, indie bands, and drinks with friends

interested in Ukrainian culture, not Ukr.ask: I'm not Ukrainian, but I'd love to learn more about Ukrainian culture and meet people. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: You might like Ukrainian, which welcomes everyone to explore the culture. You can also browse Societies to find more ways to meet people.

a mature student.ask: I'm a mature student, so I'm a bit older than most people on my course. Are there any societies you'd recommend?

shown.text: As a mature student, you might enjoy connecting with others in the Mature Students society, and you can also browse through Societies to find more groups that fit your interests.

worried about money.ask: I'm really worried about money. My loan won't last until the end of term and I don't know what to do.

shown.text: I am so sorry you are feeling worried about this. Have a look at Cost of Living, which is an NSU service that can help with money worries in one place.

run out of money for food.ask: I've run out of money for food this week and I'm not sure what to do.

shown.text: I am really sorry to hear that you are going through this. Have a look at Food Pantry and Cost of Living to help with money and food worries right now.

accused of plagiarism.ask: I've been accused of plagiarism in one of my essays and I'm panicking.

shown.text: Try not to panic, as you can get support from the Advice Centre, an NSU service that can help guide you through academic appeals and misconduct.

landlord won't fix the damp.ask: My landlord won't fix the damp in my flat and keeps ignoring my messages. Can I complain?

shown.text: Yes, you can make a complaint. The Advice Centre can help guide you on housing issues, and you can also check Rate Your Landlord to see reviews and information about student homes.

swims a lot.ask: I swim a lot and I'd like to keep it up while I'm here. Any clubs or societies?

shown.text: You might like Swimming, which is a Northumbria Sport club.

played football at school.ask: I played football at school and I'd like to start playing again. Where should I look?

shown.text: If you want to keep playing, you could try Football or Futsal. Their cards have all the details on memberships and how to join.

into ice hockey.ask: I'm really into ice hockey. Is there anything for me here?

shown.text: Since you are into ice hockey, you might like Ice Hockey, which is a great way to get involved in recreational sport.

never done sport, wants to get fit.ask: I've never really done any sport, but I want to get fitter this year. Any ideas?

shown.text: It is great to set a fitness goal. You could try Sport for various ways to stay active, Running if you want to build up stamina, or Pilates for a friendly way to build strength.

do I pay to see a doctor.ask: I'm an international student. Do I have to pay to see a doctor here?

shown.text: As an international student, you may need to pay the immigration health surcharge as part of your visa application, which covers most NHS hospital treatment. You can check the NHS Guide page for details.

how does the NHS work.ask: I've just arrived from abroad and I don't understand how the NHS works. Can you explain?

shown.text: The NHS provides healthcare in the UK, and you can register with a GP for most medical care. Have a look at our guide for more details.

shown.text: Since you love knitting and crochet, you might enjoy Stitch, Make & Bitch or Hooked By Crochet. Have a look at their cards for details.
You can find all the contact details on the cards for Stitch, Make & Bitch and Hooked By Crochet.

shown.text: Since you are into climbing and bouldering, you might enjoy Climbing, Outdoor Climbing, and Mountaineering.
You can find all the details on how to join on the cards for Climbing, Outdoor Climbing, and Mountaineering.

what a suggested society is like.ask: I like board games and tabletop role-playing games. Are there any societies for that?

shown.text: You might enjoy Gaming and Roleplay or Chess since you like board games and tabletop games.
You can check out the card for Gaming and Roleplay or Chess to see what each one is like and how to join.

shown.text: You might enjoy Film, as it is a great way to meet others who love the cinema.

notes: Loves films and going to the cinema
